title: Hashfuncs
subtitle: Fast fingerprints, buckets & cache keys.
intro: Hash SQL values with named non-cryptographic algorithms. Choose a stable representation and seed for repeatable partitioning, probabilistic-filter inputs and compact fingerprints.

reference.name: xxh3_128_hex(text [, seed])
reference.description: Canonical 32-character lowercase hex digest for strings and BLOBs.

reference.name: xxh32 / xxh64
reference.description: Classic xxHash variants, with optional seed overloads.

reference.name: murmurhash3_32 / murmurhash3_x64_128
reference.description: Named MurmurHash3 variants for explicit algorithm selection.

reference.name: spark_hash / iceberg_bucket / kafka_partition
reference.description: Reproduce Spark, Iceberg and Kafka hashing; farm_fingerprint matches BigQuery.

reference.name: jump_hash(key, buckets)
reference.description: Consistent hashing: adding a shard moves about 1/(n+1) of keys.

notes.title: Keep the representation fixed
notes.body: Match input bytes, type and seed: 0.0 and -0.0, or NaNs with different bits, hash differently, so normalize when SQL-equal values must match. Hex output is canonical high64 then low64; numeric UHUGEINT output keeps its legacy layout for stored keys.

notes.title: Collisions are possible
notes.body: Hashes are compact fingerprints, not uniqueness constraints. Retain original keys for exact equality. Use crypto for authentication or adversarial inputs.

examples.title: Route to 16 buckets
examples.sql:
SELECT i, xxh3_64(i, 42) % 16 AS bucket
FROM range(8) AS t(i);
examples.caption: The same input type and seed assign each value to the same bucket.

examples.title: Format a string fingerprint
examples.sql:
SELECT xxh3_128_hex('hello') AS digest;
-- 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters
examples.caption: Matches canonical xxHash digests from Python, Rust and C.

examples.title: Choose the output width
examples.caption: Choose the width for your collision budget and storage format.

examples.title: Match another system
examples.sql:
SELECT spark_hash('Spark', [123], 2) AS h;
-- -1321691492, as in Spark's hash()
examples.caption: For Spark bucketing use ((h % n) + n) % n; iceberg_bucket(value, n) follows the Iceberg spec.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN xxh3_128_hex('hello')='b5e9c1ad071b3e7fc779cfaa5e523818' AND typeof(xxh3_64('hello'))='UBIGINT' AND typeof(xxh3_128('hello'))='UHUGEINT' THEN true ELSE error('Hashfuncs canonical digest or width mismatch') END;
SELECT CASE WHEN spark_hash('Spark', [123], 2) = -1321691492 AND iceberg_bucket(34, 16) = iceberg_bucket(34::BIGINT, 16) THEN true ELSE error('Hashfuncs system-compatibility mismatch') END;
